name: get_engine_info
description: Returns the engine's version, platform, launch settings and package status. Call it first, to check that the engine is new enough and to see which toolchain packages are installed. It is fast and local: it never uses the network. Missing packages are installed automatically by the tools that need them, unless auto_install is off.

inputSchema.description: The get_engine_info tool takes no inputs.
inputSchema.title: GetEngineInfoInput

PackageInfo.description: A toolchain package and whether it's installed.

name.description: The package name, such as oss-cad-suite.

version.description: The package release, as a date tag (yyyy-mm-dd).

PackageStatus.description: Whether a package is ready to use.

oneOf.description:
Installed but incomplete or damaged. It is repaired when a tool needs
it, unless auto-install is off.

outputSchema.description: The engine's version, platform, launch settings and package status.

auto_install.description:
Whether the engine installs and repairs packages automatically when a
tool needs them. On by default. The host turns it off with the
--no-auto-install command-line argument.

command_line.description: The command-line arguments the engine was launched with, as given.

engine_folder.description:
The engine folder, as the host set it with the --engine-folder
command-line argument. The engine keeps its packages and logs there.

engine_version.description:
The engine release, as a date tag (yyyy-mm-dd, or yyyy-mm-dd-N for a
later release on the same day). Compare versions by date.

log_file.description:
The log file this engine process writes, in the logs subfolder of the
engine folder. Useful when reporting a problem.

packages.description: Every package in the engine's manifest, with its status.

platform.description: The platform the engine runs on, such as darwin-arm64.

protocol_versions.description: The MCP protocol versions the engine accepts, newest first.

outputSchema.title: GetEngineInfoOutput

name: install_packages
description: Installs or repairs the engine's toolchain packages, downloading them from the internet. Packages that are already installed and intact are left alone. Other tools install the packages they need on their own, so call this only to install ahead of time, such as before going offline, or when a tool returns a setup error with the install_packages action (for example when the engine was launched with automatic install turned off). A download can take a few minutes; the tool reports progress and can be cancelled.

inputSchema.description: Which packages to install or repair.

packages.description:
Names of the packages to install or repair, as get_engine_info lists
them, such as oss-cad-suite. Omitted means every package in the
engine's manifest.

inputSchema.title: InstallPackagesInput

PackageInfo.description: A toolchain package and whether it's installed.

name.description: The package name, such as oss-cad-suite.

version.description: The package release, as a date tag (yyyy-mm-dd).

PackageStatus.description: Whether a package is ready to use.

oneOf.description:
Installed but incomplete or damaged. It is repaired when a tool needs
it, unless auto-install is off.

outputSchema.description: What was installed, and every package's status afterwards.

installed.description:
Names of the packages this call installed or repaired. Empty when
they were all installed already.

packages.description: Every package in the engine's manifest, with its status.

outputSchema.title: InstallPackagesOutput
